subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should file-based internal hooks gain a supported observation-only `message:sending` event, or should pre-delivery inspection and policy remain exclusive to typed plugin hooks?
rationale: Current public guidance intentionally separates coarse internal automation from ordered, cancel-capable plugin policy, so adding this event and an alias establishes a new public hook contract that code review alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Add a narrow observer event
options.body: Support only canonical `message:sending`, emit it after successful plugin policy processing, document it as non-modifying and non-cancelling, and keep heartbeat work separate.

options.title: Keep policy plugin-only
options.body: Do not add the internal event; correct the misleading ready/validation experience and direct filtering, rewriting, and cancellation users to typed plugin hooks.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow observer event
recommendation.body: Support only canonical `message:sending`, emit it after successful plugin policy processing, document it as non-modifying and non-cancelling, and keep heartbeat work separate.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest active exact-once outbound hook design and can align this observer with existing channel and plugin ordering.
